topics.title: Types of Crafts | Identification of Crafts in the Home | Meaning (Examples) of Crafts in the Home Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS
SECOND TERM
WEEK 5
PRIMARY 1
THEME - ARTS AND CRAFTS
PREVIOUS LESSON - Meaning of Music | Importance of Music or Uses of Music in Our Society Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - TYPES OF CRAFT
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Types of Crafts
3. Identification of Crafts in the Home
4. Meaning (Examples) of Crafts in the Home
5. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. name different craft works.
2. identify different crafts in the home.
3. identify different crafts in the home.
3. define and give examples of crafts in the home.
4. produce crafts in the home.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and define craft.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of -
1. craft in the home.
2. materials and tools.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information/Read more…
- Meaning of Craft Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Cultural and Creative Arts
- Types of Crafts | Identification of Embroidery Crafts | Meaning (Examples) of Embroidery Crafts Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Cultural and Creative Arts
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Craft is an activity involving special skills in making things by hand. Display three (3) different types of craft for the pupils to examine and identify their distinct among these craft.
Pupil’s Activities - Active participation in identifying the difference among the crafts.
Teacher’s remark - Good work. All the objects represent different types of craft. Engage the pupils to make all the crafts one by one.
TYPES OF CRAFTS
There are three (3) types of crafts, namely -
1. Embroidery
2. Crafts in the home
3. Drawing of craft items
CRAFTS IN THE HOME
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Display sample of crafts in the home, if available or display charts showing crafts in the home for the pupils to identify if they have see or have one at home. Discuss and write on the the board, meaning and examples of crafts in the home.
MEANING OF CRAFT IN THE HOME
Crafts in the home are craft items or objects used for many purposes in our home. They are used for decoration, sitting, containers, etc.
For examples, crafts in the home are -
1. Wall hanger
2. Table,
3. Chair, etc.
QUICK EVALUATION
Ask pupils -
1. state 3 types of crafts.
2. What is craft in the home?
3. State 3 examples of crafts in the home.
ASSIGNMENT
Give the pupils clear photocopy of crafts in the home for them to find out how to make one.
LESSON 2 - PRODUCTION OF CRAFTS IN THE HOME
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Improvise necessary materials and tools for making crafts in the home. Guide the pupils to produce -
1. Wall hanger
- Expected improvise materials - scraw, soft wood, gum, etc.
Or
2. Doormat
- Expected improvise materials - scraw or colour cardboard and gum.
ASSIGNMENT
1. Find out the materials for drawing and painting.
2. Draw and colour a flower.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays charts showing different types of crafts.
Pupil’s Activities - Examine and identify types of crafts.
3. Shows real crafts in the home.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and describe crafts in the home.
4. Groups and guides pupils to produce crafts in the home.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the production of crafts in the home.
5. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to -
1. name 3 types of crafts.
2. describe crafts in the home.
3. give 2 examples of crafts in the home.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (Test)
1. ____________ is an activity involving special skills in making things by hand.
A. Craft
B. Drawing
C. Painting
2. The are _____ types of crafts.
A. 3
B. Three
C. A and B
3. Craft is a ____________ works.
A. Hard
B. Soft
C. Skillful
4. ____________ are real objects used for decoration and other purposes in the home.
A. Embroidery crafts
B. Drawing of crafts items
C. Crafts in the home
5. give 2 examples of crafts in the home.
- ____________
- ____________
6. Produce crafts in the home. 5 marks
Note - Number 6, as produced in the class activities.

topics.title: Singing The Nigeria National Anthem | Singing Tonic Solfa of Nigeria National Anthem Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 2 Week 2 Cultural and Creative Arts
topics.content:
CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS
SECOND TERM
WEEK 2
PRIMARY 1
THEME - PERFORMING ARTS AND ENTERTAINMENT

TOPIC - INTRODUCTION TO SINGING
LEARNING AREA

PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. pronounce each word of the song correctly as they repeat after the teacher.
2. Sing the tonic solfas.
3. Sing the text of the song.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can sing National Anthem.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. CD player
2. Phones for playing songs, etc.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION (HISTORY)
A national anthem is a song that represents its people, history, and values. It brings people together and makes them feel proud when celebrating their country as a whole.
A national anthem is a nation’s official song that is used by a nation on public or state occasions.
The anthem was composed in 1978 to replaced the previous national anthem, “Nigeria, We Hail Thee”.
The Nigerian national anthem were composed by five people:
1. P. O. Aderibigbe
2. John A. Ilechukwu
3. Dr. Sota Omoigui
4. Eme tim Akpan, and
5. B.A. Ogunnaike.
Nigerian National anthem has two verses. The first is mostly sung while the second verse is recited as “The National Prayer”.
NIGERIAN NATIONAL ANTHEM
FIRST ANTHEM,
Arise, O Compatriots
Nigeria’s Call Obey
To serve our fatherland
With love and strength and faith
The labour of our heroes past,
shall never be in vain
To serve with heart and might,
One Nation bound in freedom, peace and unity.
Be sure that, the pupils pronounce each word of the song correctly.
LESSON 2 - SINGING TONIC SOLFAS OF NATIONAL ANTHEM
d: (Do), s: (Sol), l: (La) r: (Re) and m: (Mi)
SECOND ANTHEM
Arise, O compatriots                             s: d: s: d m: s:
Nigeria’s call obey                                 m: f: m: r: r: d:
To serve our Fatherland                       s: d: s: d: m: s:
With love and strength and faith         m: f: m: r: r: d:
The labour of our heroes past             r: r: m: f: r: m: f: s:
shall never be in vain                             s: l: s: f: m: r:
To serve with heart and might             d: s: s: s: m: l:
One nation bound in freedom              r: r: m: f: r: l: s:
peace and unity                                      f: m: r: r: d:
Note - Please, you call on the music teacher(s) for support.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher plays children’s songs that lead pupils to sing and get excited.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils singing Nigerian National Anthem.
3. Teacher uses the National anthem song to introduce the lesson and guides pupils to sing it with the correct words.
4. Teacher leads pupils to sing tonic solfas of Singing Nigerian National Anthem.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils repeat after the teacher.
5. Teacher summarizes the lesson on the board with appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils participate actively in the lesson summary by responding correctly to most of the questions and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Types of Crafts | Identification of Embroidery Crafts | Meaning (Examples) of Embroidery Crafts Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Cultural and Creative Arts

Teacher asks pupils to:
1. pronounce each word of the song correctly as they repeat after the teacher.
2. Sing the tonic solfas.
3. Sing the text of the song.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Craft is the making useful things by hands. When you make things with your hands, they are called craft.
We can use our hands to make different crafts.
TYPES OF CRAFTS
There are three (3) types of crafts, namely -
1. Embroidery
2. Crafts in the home
3. Drawing of craft items
MEANING OF EMBROIDERY CRAFTS
Embroidery crafts are crafts made on clothes using materials such as needle and thread.
For examples, embroidery crafts are -
1. Table cloth
2. Handkerchief
3. Small purse, etc.
LESSON 2 - MAKING SIMPLE EMBROIDERY CRAFTS
MATERIALS NEEDED - fabric, paper embroidery patterns, pencil, embroidery needle, embroidery thread in colors, scissors, wooden embroidery hoop, twine or ribbon.
GUIDELINES
1. Cut a piece of fabric so that it is about one inch bigger than your embroidery hoop on all sides.
2. Trace your design onto your fabric with a pencil.
3. Put your fabric into the embroidery hoop so it is nice and tight.
4. Thread your first color of embroidery thread into a needle and make a small knot at the end. Starting on the backside of your fabric, pull your thread through the fabric where your design starts.
5. Stitch along the hand-drawn design, leaving a small space between each stitch.
6. Cut the excess fabric around your embroidery hoop.
For sample and pictures, visit - 9 Simple Embroidery Designs

CULTURAL AND CREATIVE ARTS
SECOND TERM
WEEK 6
PRIMARY 1
THEME - PERFORMING ARTS AND ENTERTAINMENT
PREVIOUS LESSON - Definition to Dance | Types of Dance | Importance of Dance in Our School and Society Primary 1 (Basic 1) Term 2 Week 5 Cultural and Creative Arts
TOPIC - INTRODUCTION TO STORYTELLING
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Storytelling
3. Makes Up Short Story
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. identify a story line in a story or folktale.
2. create or make up a short story.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can made up a story from story pictures book.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of stories in a book; Illustrations of characters in the story; Television; Video tapes and CDs.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Storytelling is the description of social and cultural activity that happened in the past.
It is also the art of telling or writing about past. Storytelling can be verbal, written or in picture.
REASONS FOR STORYTELLING
People tell stories for the following reasons -
1. To teach us moral value and lesson.
2. To entertain us.
3. To educate us about our environment.
4. To caution us about our behaviours.
5. To respect one another.
6. To reserve our culture.
7. To tolerate one another.
LESSON 2 - MAKE UP A SHORT STORY
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities
Making up a story line with any one or two of the following themes - tolerance, service to the nation, truthfulness, respect, obedience, etc. Or follow the link to choose stories - Nigerian Fairy Tales, Folk Tales and Fables
LESSON 3 - REVISION AND WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
As stated in the performance objectives or lesson evaluation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes the pupils into groups depending on the size of the class.
3. Teacher gives each group a story pictures book. Note, the book must not be same.
4. Teacher asks pupils as groups to make up a story from the book with appropriate title.
5. Teacher uses the pupil’s relevant responses to introduce the lesson and lead a class discussion on the meaning of storytelling based on their activities.
6. Teacher develops a story line idea - obedience and make up a short story around it.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils follow story line on obedience
7. Teacher leads and guides pupils to tell a story based on their environment, events or things they watch on television.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils tell story based on their environment, events or things they watch on television.
8. The teacher summarizes the lesson on the board using appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils participate actively in the summary of the lesson by responding correctly to most of the questions and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Second Term Mid Term Test Cultural and Creative Arts for Primary 1
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils to -
1. explain the meaning of storytelling.
2. state 3 reasons for telling a story.
3. tell a story based on obedience and respect.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT
ATTEMPT ALL THE QUESTIONS
Weekly Assessment should be based on the make up stories or story lines.

ENTRY BEHAVIOUR

INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS

METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.

2. National Curriculum for SSS Classes

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION (MEANING OF RECORDER)
Recorder is a musical instrument made of wood or plastic that produces sound.
The wooden recorder is the most preferable by the professionals while the plastic is common amongst the beginners. Wooden recorder can be made with different types of wood to give different sounds.
USES OF A RECORDER
The uses of recorder are as follows:
1. It teaches us to read music.
2. It is used for teaching music beginners.
3. It is used developing eyes and hands coordination.
4. It is used for sight reading and developing listening skills.
5. It is used developing strong lungs and breath control.
6. It is used for developing our listening skills.
7. It is used for developing our musical ear.
8. It is used for playing vocal music and other parts of musical instrument.
LESSON 2 - STEPS OF PLAYING THE RECORDER
There are five easy steps to master the recorder,
1. Get or purchase a recorder
2. Learn how to hold the recorder and blow to make sound.
3. Learn correct tonguing technique.
4. Learn the fingering chart.
5. Practice makes perfect!
Reference - West Music
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the students some questions; then, the teacher -
2. Teacher organizes the pupils into groups depending on the size of the class.
3. Teacher displays chart showing different types of recorder (wooden and plastic recorders).
4. Teacher asks the pupils as group to identify and describe the contents of the chart. Note, most of the pupils will identify the recorder as whistle. Use it to introduce the lesson - recorder.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils identify and describe the recorder.
5. Teacher uses the chart and pupil’s relevant responses to introduce and leads a class discussion on  the meaning of recorder.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils pay attention to the lesson introduction and participate actively in the class discussion.
6. Teacher displays sample sample of recorders, guides the pupils to hold, place the fingers correctly on the record and blow.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils hold, place the fingers correctly on the record and blow.
7. Teacher leads a class discussion on the uses of recorder.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils analyze the importance of recorder as a musical instrument.
8. Teacher summarizes the lesson on the board by using appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils participate actively in the lesson summary by responding correctly to most of the questions and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

1. define a recorder.
2. state 3 uses of recorder.

A. Radio
B. Mp3

A. Plastic recorder
B. Musical recorder

A. Master2
B. Beginners

4. Wooden recorder is the most preferable by the ______.

B. Students

THEME - ARTS AND CRAFTS

TOPIC - SENSE OF BELONGINGS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Sense of Belongings
3. Importance of Sense of Belongings
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain the sense of belongings.
2. state the importance of sense of belongings.
3. mention some items that can be personal.
4. list some items that cannot be personal.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and state things that belong to them.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of pictures or charts of community development and programme.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Sense of belonging is the feeling of been an important member of an entity.
This is different from personal belonging. Personal belongings are items that belong one person alone. Mostly, the things that cannot be share with others.
Things that can be personal are as follows:
1. Clothes
2. Shoes
3. Toothbrush
4. Underwear, etc.
SENSE OF BELONGINGS
Sense of belonging is when people feels connected to other peoples at home, school or community to share responsibility for the betterment of themselves. That’s, knowing where and with whom you belong are -
1. Family
2. Culture
3. School
4. Community
5. Group or class
6. Tribe
7. Religion
8. Association, etc.
LESSON 2 - IMPORTANCE OF SENSE OF BELONGINGS
The importance of sense of belongings are -
1. It improves quality of life.
2. It make us feel secure and protected.
3. We are not alone.
4. We have all necessary support and assistance.
5. Growth and development.
HOW TO ACHIEVE SENSE OF BELONGINGS
There are several ways to achieve sense of belongings -
1. Active participation
2. Be open minded
3. Making an effort
4. Be mindful of other
5. Think before you act
6. Voluntary contribution
7. Be yourself always
8. Share your passions and interests
9. Practice acceptance
10. Practice tolerance
LESSON 3 - REVISION AND WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
As stated in the performance objectives or lesson evaluation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes the pupils into groups depending on the size of the class.
3. Teacher asks the pupils to state what they like and enjoy most in their among their family members, school and the community.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils state and discuss the benefits of been member of a family, school and the community.
4. Teacher uses the pupils relevant responses to introduce the lesson and display chart showing community development and programme such environmental sanitation, training the young ones, etc. for the them to examine and discuss.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils pay attention to the lesson introduction, examine and discuss the contents of the chart.
5. Teacher uses the chart to lead a class discussion on the meaning of sense of belongings and its importance.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils participate actively in the class discussion, explain and analyze the importance of sense of belongings in their lives.
6. Teacher summarizes the lesson on the board using appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils participate actively in the lesson summary by responding correctly to most of the questions and write as instructs.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON

LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Examples of Craft Items
3. Drawing of Craft Items at Home and in the Society
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain the meaning of craft items.
2. give examples of craft item at home and in the school.
3. draw some craft items.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and state different craft items at home and in the school.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of -
1. sample of some craft items.
2. pictures of craft item.
3. pencil, crayons, drawing books and ruler.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Craft is the making useful things by hands.
When you make things with your hands, that things are known as craft.
Crafts are used for beautification and other purposes in our home, school and office. Some of the items such as chairs, tables, hangers, curtains, containers, etc. used in home, schools, offices and other places are made of Craft items.
We can use our hands to make different crafts such as
1. Hand fan
2. Crown
3. Beads
4. embroidery, etc.
MEANING OF CRAFT ITEMS
Craft Items are items made with hand. Craft items are made by weaving, carving, or pottery.
Most of the craft items are now economical and highly valuable in this modern day.
MEANING OF DRAWING OF CRAFT ITEMS
Drawing of craft items are visual art on paper using drawing materials and tools. It is also known as drawing and painting crafts.
LESSON 2 - DRAWING OF DIFFERENT CRAFT ITEMS
Examples of craft items at home and in the classroom -
1. Beads
2. Local mats
3. Local clay pots
4. Leather products
5. Batik tie and dye
6. Calabash craft
7. Basket weaving
8. Bag weaving
9. Pottery
10. Woven cloths - Aṣọ-òkè, Akwete Cloth, Saki cloth and Parmala cloth, etc.
DRAWING OF CRAFT ITEMS
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Teacher provides necessary drawing materials and tools, and asks the pupils to draw any of the displayed craft items.
LESSON 3 - DRAWING OF CRAFT ITEMS
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes the pupils into groups depending on the size of the class.
3. Teacher displays sample of craft items at home and in the school and as well as chart showing them.
4. Teacher allows the people to identify, examine and describe them.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils identify craft items at home and in the school.
5. Teachers uses the craft items and the pupil’s relevant responses to introduce the lesson.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils appreciate the ideas of real craft items and their drawings.
6. Teacher shows illustrations of craft items and leads a class discussion on the meaning and drawing of craft items.
Pupil’s Activities - The pay attention to the lesson introduction to understand the concept of lessons.
7. Teacher leads and guides the pupils as groups to draw craft items.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils draw craft items.and apply appropriate colour to their drawings.
8. Teacher summarizes the lesson on the board using appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils participate actively in the lesson summary by responding correctly to most of the questions and write as instructs.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain what music is.
2. state the importance of music.
ENTRY BEHAVIOURS
The pupils can understand what music is.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Radio set with cassette or flash containing songs
2. Mobile phone for playing music
3. Mp3 player
4. Musical instruments
5. Chart Showing songs
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.

9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum

All Relevant Material

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION (MEANING OF MUSIC)
Music is a group of sound that people listen to and enjoy.
There are types of sound - pleasant and unpleasant sound. Music is a pleasant sound.
Music can be voices or instruments. People clapped, moved their body and tapped their feet while listening to music.
USES OF MUSIC IN OUR SOCIETY
Music is very important part of our society because
1. It is a universal language for all creatures - communication.
2. It is an important tool for entertainment.
3. It unites people together.
4. It is for pleasure.
5. It helps people to relax.
6. It help people to focus at work, etc.
LESSON 2 - REVISION OF LESSON 1
As stated in Lesson 1.
LESSON 3 - WEEKLY ASSESSMENT (TEST)
As stated in performance objectives or lesson evaluation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Teacher organizes the pupils into groups depending on the size of the class.
3. Teacher gets a small mp3 prayer and earpiece each of the groups or mobile phone.
4. Teacher plays the mp3 player or mobile device for the pupils to listen for 2 to 3 minutes.
5. Teacher asks these questions -
- What are you listening to?
- What do you like or enjoy in the music?
- Why do people listen to music?
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils respond correctly the questions in activity.
6. Teacher uses the above activities and pupil’s responses introduce the lesson and creates other activities that will lead to the concept of music.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils participate actively in the lesson introduction, create and preform other activities such as clapping, beating two more objects to make a sound, etc.
7. Teacher leads a class discussion on the music and uses of music in our society.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils explain the meaning of music, appreciate and analyze the uses of music in our society.
8. Summarizes the lesson on the board using appropriate lesson evaluation.
Pupil’s Activities - The pupils participate actively in the lesson summary by responding correctly to most of the lesson and write as instructed.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
